swarm_field_from_piv — DRIVE swarmflow op

• Data kinds: any × scalar × scalar → table

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.swarm_field_from_piv(frames, res: 'float', frame_dt: 'float', center=(0.0, 0.0), window: 'int' = 24, overlap: 'float' = 0.5, min_peak_ratio: 'float' = 1.1, outlier_threshold=3.0) -> 'dict' (to call the implementation directly, import swarmflow; swarmflow.swarm_field_from_piv(frames, res: 'float', frame_dt: 'float', center=(0.0, 0.0), window: 'int' = 24, overlap: 'float' = 0.5, min_peak_ratio: 'float' = 1.1, outlier_threshold=3.0) -> 'dict'; from the registry, opsdrive.get("swarm_field_from_piv"))

• GPU: none (CPU reference implementation only)

Usage

Overhead frame sequence → PIV by cross-correlation of neighboring frames (pivops.piv_cross_correlate) → average over all pairs → velocity field in the world.

It does not distinguish individuals one by one (so it works even with overlaps), but fluctuations finer than the window (window px) are smoothed out. Windows whose peak ratio is below min_peak_ratio are missing (NaN). ★Swarms tend to line up like a lattice (pushing evens out the spacing), so correlation peaks also appear at neighbouring lattice positions and the peak ratio is close to 1. Measured (spacing 7.5 px, window 24): with threshold 0, mismatched windows creep in and the rms against individual velocities is 13.7 % of U; with 1.1 it is 1.9 % (85 % of windows measured); with 1.3 the measured windows drop to 18 % —— the default is 1.1. In addition, a per-pair normalised median test (pivops.piv_outlier_mask, threshold outlier_threshold, None to skip) marks outlying windows as missing before averaging. Following pivops' caution, 3 is used, looser than the customary 2, so that steep gradients (shoulders of obstacles) are not called outliers. The pivops components (dy, dx) [px/frame] are converted to u = dx·res/Δt, v = −dy·res/Δt.

Returns:

dict of the velocity field + valid_fraction (fraction of windows measured), n_pairs.
